title: A cloud session on a child repo gets claude-settings with its git history, so compliance-check can name the parent commit
why: In a cloud session on ios-adblock, the session-start refresh got HTTP 403 when it fetched the claude-settings tarball, so /root/claude-settings was a copy with no .git and compliance-check stopped at step 1, unable to name the parent commit.
note: Coordinator, Oct 29 14:41 CDT. claude-settings is public, so the 403 is likely the cloud proxy, not a private repo. Fix: the cloud refresh gets claude-settings by git clone, or another route the proxy allows, so every child-repo session has a known parent commit. Red first: a refresh in a cloud session on a child repo leaves /root/claude-settings with no .git. Workaround meanwhile: the r1 lanes attach claude-settings with add_repo. Needs no answer. Port: no (the refresh lives here). Placed ahead of r1 (triage 12, Oct 29): every r1 visit in the cloud hits it.
